reports.title: Fishing Scene Awaits Fall's Arrival
reports.text:
A few crappie have been taken in the 11 to 14 foot depth range in early morning and late afternoons when lowlight conditions aid the bite.
Some are using live minnows exclusively and scoring a few reluctant crappie to bite.
The bass bite has also been sluggish due to slow current and a lack of cloud cover on the hot days. In the early morning hours and perhaps late afternoon the bite has been the best. Those bright sunny days when the sun is bearing down and daytime highs are in the mid 90’s has made it tough out there. A few bass were on shallow gravel banks in early morning hours and just before dark. Tossing topwater and shallow running shad colored crankbaits have accounted for a few…

reports.title: Bass Techniques for Heat Wave on Kentucky Lake
reports.text:
Bass Techniques for Heat Wave on Kentucky Lake
Last year the August heat wave slowed down the progression of shad moving to the shallow flats and also slowed down the bass feeding in the shallow flat water. This year the shad and bass are feeding well in the shallow flats even with the heat wave. I have a few places where bass are feeding all day in super shallow water even with the sun up and high.
I typically fish water that is 3 foot to 6 inches when I am going after the shallow bass that August 1st brings us.
The summer largemouth ledge fishing on Kentucky Lake starts getting tougher during the end of July but there are still super deep ledge fish in August and shallow ledge fish.

reports.title: Early Mornings and Late Afternoons are Providing the Best Bites.
reports.text:
A 15 1/2” crappie was her best to go along with other crappie, several bass, catfish and a bucket full of nice yellow bass.
Neither had ever trolled for crappie but both were quick learners and a joy to fish with. The fish cooperated and their catch was anchored by a 16 1/2” & 15 1/2” crappie, the larger for the son and personal bests for both. The rest of the catch was crappie and yellow bass. Both giant crappie came on Pico Lures Beachball pattern.
Crappie are still being caught by those using forward facing sonar. Many of the deeper structures are full of very small crappie or yellow bass.
Doug Wynn is a professional guide on Kentucky Lake and specializes in crappie fishing.
